LESSON: MELODY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.5: Melody

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Melody. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can interesting melodies be created?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody
2. state the qualities of a good melody as a foundation to composition
3. create short melodies using the sol-fa syllables d, r and m
4. model clay slabs with sol-fa syllables using coil and slab techniques
5. enjoy creating short melodies and modelling using clay. • roll clay into slab and cut out three rectangular pieces of three different sizes, • model so-lfa syllables (d r m) using coil technique and attach on the slabs

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MELODY
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Melody helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MELODY
Study Melody like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody

What this means
In this part you learn to identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Melody is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Melody in your own words. (skill: state the qualities of a good melody as a foundation to composition)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: create short melodies using the sol-fa syllables d, r and m)

Example 4: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: model clay slabs with sol-fa syllables using coil and slab techniques)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Melody to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody.
3. Practise this skill: state the qualities of a good melody as a foundation to composition.
4. Practise this skill: create short melodies using the sol-fa syllables d, r and m.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Melody from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Melody: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Melody?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can interesting melodies be created?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Melody means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody.
5. Be able to: state the qualities of a good melody as a foundation to composition.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
